opps.title: Coors Light — 17% of your commission, down 10% YoY
opps.body: Sales are down 773 cases (10%) vs last year, but Coors Light is still 17.1% of your total commission — your #2 brand. That decline has already cost about $773 in modeled commission, and recovering half of it is worth roughly $386. On a brand this size that is a bigger swing than anything you could realistically open new this year. 193 accounts bought it last year; 180 have this year — 13 accounts stopped carrying it.

opps.title: 7 accounts stopped ordering — $526 of commission gone quiet
opps.body: Each of these bought from you last year and has ordered nothing at all in 2026. A lost account is the most expensive kind of decline: there is no brand mix to fix and nothing replaces it automatically — the whole relationship has stopped. The largest, Hilton Meadowlnd E Ruth, was worth 147 cases last year on its own. These are the calls with the shortest path back to commission, because the account already knows you.

opps.title: 8 accounts holding all year but soft this month — 169 cases behind
opps.body: Year to date each of these is fine, so the relationship is not the problem — but month to date they are all well behind where they were last August. That is the pattern that becomes a bad quarter if nobody catches it, and it is the cheapest kind to fix: the account is still buying, it just has not placed its usual order yet. Together they are 169 cases and about $169 of commission behind last August's pace, with days left in the month to close it.
